# Error-sheet feedback

Counts are unique adjudicated local changes against either witness, not rates per token. Classes overlap; each place is counted once within a class. The primary classes use the recorded change kind and normalized error tags. The finer classes below use explicit row-by-row reviews of C, H, the final reading and the recorded ink evidence; mere occurrence of a feature elsewhere in a row is not a correction. A zero means no reviewed correction in that class, not that the feature is absent from the source.

All 570 current change places have an explicit classification review; no fine-category count is inferred from a missing tag.

Review records and category scopes: `verification/feedback_classification_025_039.json`, `verification/feedback_classification_040_046.json`.

## Local refinements to the error sheet

The recurring problems fall within the sheet's existing classes; the following refinements describe how they manifested here rather than proposing unsupported new error rates.

1. **Reading a shared type cell and ordering its impressions are separate tasks.** Reciprocal letter pairs can be visible in adjacent cells even when the final word is linguistically obvious. Examples include the first chaines and longueur on041, article e/a layers on039, and several corrected words on033–038. Mark the whole old/new pair uncertain when chronology is uncertain. A doubt attached only to the old glyph would overstate the standing layer.
2. **Cancellation devices can occupy blank spaces.** Rows of keyed x marks pass through interword blanks as well as letters. Recover the underlying text when possible, but do not create lexical x characters in those blank cells. Examples include the long cancelled phrase on041 and the cancellations on039–040.
3. **A constructed mathematical glyph is not automatically a correction.** The two tensor signs on041 are keyed O+x constructions. Opposite-category o and small zero-position o indices elsewhere are machine forms to record consistently, with the visible upper/lower revision state retained separately.
4. **Source-edge loss differs from a crop boundary.** The first can remain unresolved; the second requires a boundary-completion view. Crops on039 completed the underlined important, the hand insertion and its mathematical endpoints, and the grou-/pes and cer-/taines breaks. The clipped lower diagram fragment on040 has no recoverable continuation outside the scan.
5. **Reference strokes and source punctuation need separate classification.** A loop with a shaft can be a reference mark, and a long unheaded bracket can group lines without supplying parentheses to the running sentence. Count suspension points locally; a faint dash-shaped point can still be one of a written sequence.

The hand log records local scope and exceptions. No source spelling or mathematical slip was silently harmonized merely because the same object is written more conventionally elsewhere.

6. **A frame can enclose a live typed word while carrying an insertion.** On046 the long generator-note frame surrounds the live connue; its continuation beneath the typed points does not cross the word. On045 both ends of the top addition are continuous framing/leader strokes. Their shape must be assessed together with attachment, not reduced to a count of apparent parentheses.
7. **Count physical cells before completing a familiar word.** On045 remp + one l/a cell + çant has no separate extra a cell. On046 the p between the raised typed words is an independent uncancelled impression. Neither is repaired from the expected phrase.
8. **Editorial notation conventions are separate from source disagreements.** H’s regular low-point and bold-category macro forms are not counted merely because this edition records baseline points and actual underlines. An exceptional absence of an underline, missing prime, wrong label side, or absent source point is still collated from the ink.
